item: row 391: the write-gate phase tests wait for the holder's statement to reach the driver, never a fixed 0.25 s
summary: The watchdog-sample test read 'pool-wait' instead of 'execute' on a loaded CI runner (24 Nov, Core-only shard 2 of PR #2347): _Holder slept a fixed 0.25 s and assumed the holder had checked out its connection and was inside SELECT pause by then. pause() now sets an event as it starts; a holder whose body runs a statement waits on it (bounded, 10 s, a named assert) and then 0.1 s more so the hold is past HOLD_RECORD_S and is journalled. The two statement tests use it; the pool-wait and Python-phase holders keep the short sleep, since they wait on nothing SQL. Test-only: no source change. Eight runs green, five more under six busy CPU loops.
